instruction:
Three-software CAE flow: AutoCAD -> SolidWorks -> Abaqus/CAE. No init files are provided; start from blank files.

Chain evidence requirement: use the design token EW_ACAD_SW_ABQ_03. In AutoCAD, add a readable label containing EW_ACAD_SW_ABQ_03 and AUTOCAD_TO_SOLIDWORKS on a CHAIN layer in stage1_profile.dxf. In SolidWorks, keep EW_ACAD_SW_ABQ_03, FROM_stage1_profile.dxf, and SOLIDWORKS_TO_ABAQUS encoded in the part/custom properties or STEP export metadata so the text of stage2_geometry.step contains them. In Abaqus/CAE, create at least one model, part, instance, set, surface, job description, or other native name containing both EW_ACAD_SW_ABQ_03 and IMPORTED_FROM_stage2_geometry.step, so the final CAE file carries evidence that Abaqus consumed the SolidWorks STEP handoff.

1. In AutoCAD, use drawing tools to create the 2D profile and save it as C:\Users\user\Desktop\stage1_profile.dxf. Draw an 80 mm x 60 mm base outline on layer OUTLINE and four D5 mounting-hole circles on layer HOLE.
2. In SolidWorks, import stage1_profile.dxf and create the 3D part. Extrude a 5 mm base, add ten parallel fins 16 mm high, and export C:\Users\user\Desktop\stage2_geometry.step.
3. In Abaqus/CAE, import stage2_geometry.step and create the thermal finite-element model. Use the model name Model-HeatPlateThermal. Define material Aluminum with conductivity about 170 W/m-K, create a section using Aluminum, and assign it to the heat plate. Create a steady heat transfer step named Step-Thermal. Create a set named HEAT_PAD and a surface named FIN_SURFACES. Use first-order heat-transfer elements such as DC3D8 where practical or coarse DC3D4 where needed. Mesh the fins with a coarse swept or structured mesh, using only the divisions needed to represent the fin thickness and height and avoiding local fin refinement. Create a heat flux load named HeatFlux-Base on the bottom heat pad. Create a convection interaction or equivalent boundary condition named BC-Convection on FIN_SURFACES. Submit the job named Job-HeatPlateThermal and wait for the analysis to complete.
4. Required deliverables on the Desktop: C:\Users\user\Desktop\stage1_profile.dxf, C:\Users\user\Desktop\stage2_geometry.step, C:\Users\user\Desktop\Job-HeatPlateThermal.cae, and C:\Users\user\Desktop\Job-HeatPlateThermal.odb. Do not create extra STEP, DXF, CAE, or ODB deliverables.

 First use AutoCAD to create the DXF profile, then use SolidWorks to import the DXF and export the STEP file, then use Abaqus/CAE to import that STEP file, build the finite-element model, submit the job, and save the CAE and ODB deliverables. Software launch locations: SOLIDWORKS 2025: `C:\Users\Public\Desktop\SOLIDWORKS 2025.lnk`; Abaqus/CAE: `C:\Users\user\Desktop\Abaqus CAE.lnk`; AutoCAD 2024 (English): `C:\Users\Public\Desktop\AutoCAD 2024 - English.lnk`.
